summary: CCC lookout on Bear Mountain, moved to the Calaveras fairgrounds in 1986-87 and ordered torn down in 2004; one listing still shows it standing.

facts.design: Register: 41-foot steel tower with a 14-foot square cab, built 1987-88 on a Plesha design; the same page describes the demolished tower as a 1930s CCC timber tower
facts.status_note: Calaveras County Fair Board ordered it demolished in 2004 (register and Feb 2004 news report). The Forest Fire Lookout Association California list still shows it standing.
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire)

access.note: Ordered torn down in 2004. No source read confirms a tower at the fairgrounds that the public can visit.

visit.trail_note: No source confirms a tower left to climb. Ask the Calaveras County Fair before going to the fairgrounds.

events.note: CCC built the original three-story timber tower on Bear Mountain. Register gives 1933 or 1936; a 2008 obituary says a crew member helped build it in 1938.
Renamed Fowler Peak Lookout for Oliver E. Fowler, a Stanislaus National Forest ranger
Moved to the Calaveras County Fairgrounds in Angels Camp in 1986-87 when CDF decided to replace it. Re-erection was under way in November 1986.
Register: 41-foot steel tower with a 14-foot cab, built 1987-88 at about $70,000. Its site, and whether it still stands, are not clear in the sources read.
Fair board ordered demolition. Inmate crews from the Vallecito Conservation Camp were scheduled to start razing it on Feb 17, 2004.

corrections.why: The register describes the fairgrounds tower as demolished, and the fair board ordered it torn down in 2004 with razing set for Feb 17, 2004. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list and a 2008 obituary still say it stands; see resolved_conflicts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1933 or 1936. The 2004 news report gives 1936, citing a May 1987 Calaveras Enterprise article. A 2008 obituary gives 1938 for a crew member's work. The story gives the range and cites each.
The register names State Forester O.E. Fowler. The 2004 news report names Oliver E. Fowler, a Stanislaus National Forest ranger. The sources read do not link the two, and the story says so.

The register and the 2004 news report say demolition was ordered or under way. The FFLA California list and a 2008 obituary say it stands. The record uses removed and the story reports the disagreement.

sources.title: Calaveras Fairgrounds Tower To Come Tumbling Down
sources.publisher: myMotherLode.com (Calaveras Enterprise story by Craig Koscho; byline Bill Johnson)

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'standing' corrected to removed: the register and the Feb 2004 news report both point to demolition, but the FFLA list and the 2008 obituary ('where it stands today') disagree, and no post-2008 source was read. A site check or a call to the Calaveras County Fair would settle it. The register's design text mixes a 1987-88 steel tower with a demolished CCC timber tower on one page; the story does not pick one. No staffing or fire history appears in the sources read. The Mother Lode article's 'Published Feb 17, 2004' date is the same day as the razing start. One WebSearch returned a summary claim that the 1936 original was first called Bear Mountain Lookout; that claim is in the Mother Lode article, which was read directly. No photos added.
